title: 🧠 Neuralink Chip Controls Grok with Imagined Speech... and the Patient Calls His Wife with His Thoughts!
body: 🧠 Neuralink Chip Controls Grok with Imagined Speech... and the Patient Calls His Wife with His Thoughts!

On October 29, Neuralink revealed a new demonstration unlike anything before it: a participant in its clinical trials, who has lived with ALS for 7 years, controlled the Grok AI agent using only imagined speech, without saying a single word out loud.

The method is that the participant imagines saying "Hey Neuralink" followed by the command, and Grok wakes up and carries out computer tasks on its own. The demonstration also showed new technology that automatically detects neural speech activity, starting and stopping transcription without a button, a live display of neural signals during speech, neural speech input directly into phone calls, as the participant called his wife from his phone using his thoughts, as well as a neural dictation keyboard at the iOS system level and improvements to the Bloom app.

All of this was built during a 72-hour engineering sprint at the participant's home, producing 8 prototypes. The company says it is "early exploration," with no figures on accuracy or response speed, and the chips are still experimental and have not yet received approval from the US Food and Drug Administration.

Simply put: when imagined speech becomes commands for an AI agent and phone calls, the brain itself becomes the computer interface; do you think this technology will restore independence to people who have lost the ability to speak and move, or is the road to everyday use still long?
